intro_en: So far you have spoken only in the polite です / ます style. In this lesson you will learn the plain style (普通形) used with friends, family and people younger than you. It is like the difference in Tamil between "நீங்கள் வருகிறீர்களா?" (are you coming? polite) and "நீ வர்றியா?" (you coming? casual). You will learn the four plain forms (present/past × positive/negative) of verbs, い-adjectives, な-adjectives and nouns, how to ask questions, けど (but), and dropping particles in speech, always comparing them side by side with the polite forms.

g20-1.explanation_en: Japanese has two speech styles: (1) 丁寧形, the polite です / ます style, used with teachers, superiors, people you meet for the first time, shopkeepers and so on. (2) 普通形, the plain style, used with close friends, family and people younger than you, and also in diaries and some writing. It is just like the difference between "நீங்கள்" and "நீ" in Tamil, as in "நீங்கள் சாப்பிட்டீர்களா?" vs "நீ சாப்பிட்டியா?" (have you eaten? polite vs casual), so the idea is already familiar to Tamil speakers. The meaning doesn't change; only the closeness of the relationship changes. If in doubt, use the polite style; speaking plainly to a stranger sounds rude. Also, from Lesson 21 on, the plain form is required inside patterns such as 〜と思います and 〜時, so this lesson is very important.
g20-1.tamil_parallel_en: Like the Tamil நீங்கள் / நீ split: நீங்கள் நாளை வருகிறீர்களா? ("will you come tomorrow?", polite) / நீ நாளைக்கு வர்றியா? ("you coming tomorrow?", casual) = 明日来ますか。／明日来る？
g20-1.formation_en: Polite style (丁寧形): 〜ます / 〜です: teachers, superiors, strangers ; Plain style (普通形): dictionary form / ない / た / なかった, adjective + (だ): friends, family, younger people
g20-1.pitfalls_en: It is better not to mix polite and plain styles in the same conversation. Asking a teacher わかった？ is like calling your teacher "நீ" (casual "you") in Tamil.

g20-2.explanation_en: A verb has four polite forms: ます / ません / ました / ませんでした. Each has a plain partner, and you have already learned three of them: ます → dictionary form (Lesson 18), ません → ない-form (Lesson 17), ました → た-form (Lesson 19). Only one is new: ませんでした → なかった. Because ない behaves like an い-adjective, ない → なかった, just like 寒い → 寒かった (行かない → 行かなかった). These are like the shortened spoken Tamil forms "போகிறேன் → போறேன்" (I go), "போனேன் → போனேன்" (I went), "போகவில்லை → போகல" (didn't go). The plain forms of あります are ある / ない / あった / なかった.
g20-2.tamil_parallel_en: Like the four basic Tamil verb forms: போகிறேன் / போகவில்லை / போனேன் / போகவில்லை (past) ("go / don't go / went / didn't go") = 行く / 行かない / 行った / 行かなかった.
g20-2.formation_en: Polite → plain: ます→dictionary (行きます→行く) ; ません→ない (行きません→行かない) ; ました→た (行きました→行った) ; ませんでした→なかった (行きませんでした→行かなかった). Group I 書く: 書く・書かない・書いた・書かなかった / Group II 食べる: 食べる・食べない・食べた・食べなかった / Group III する: する・しない・した・しなかった ; 来る: 来る(くる)・来ない(こない)・来た(きた)・来なかった(こなかった) / ある: ある・ない・あった・なかった
g20-2.pitfalls_en: The plain form of ありません is not ×あらない but ○ない. 来なかった = こなかった (not きなかった). Don't combine ない + でした as in ×行かないでした; it is ○行かなかった.

g20-3.explanation_en: The plain style for い-adjectives is very easy: just drop です from the polite form. 大きいです → 大きい、大きくないです → 大きくない、大きかったです → 大きかった、大きくなかったです → 大きくなかった. You already learned these forms in Lessons 8 and 12, so there is nothing new to memorise; です is only a polite decoration. It is like shortening "பெரியதாக இருக்கிறது" (it is big) to "பெருசு" (big) in spoken Tamil. For いい: いい / よくない / よかった / よくなかった. Don't add だ after an い-adjective (×大きいだ).
g20-3.tamil_parallel_en: Like the four Tamil forms of an adjective: பெரிது / பெரிதில்லை / பெரிதாக இருந்தது / பெரிதாக இல்லை ("big / not big / was big / wasn't big") = 大きい / 大きくない / 大きかった / 大きくなかった.
g20-3.formation_en: Drop です: 大きいです→大きい ; 大きくないです→大きくない ; 大きかったです→大きかった ; 大きくなかったです→大きくなかった. いい: いい・よくない・よかった・よくなかった. つまらない: つまらない・つまらなくない・つまらなかった・つまらなくなかった
g20-3.pitfalls_en: Don't put だ after an い-adjective, as in ×可愛いだ or ×寒いだ. The past of いい is not ×いかった but ○よかった.

g20-4.explanation_en: な-adjectives and nouns change in the same way: です → だ、じゃありません → じゃない、でした → だった、じゃありませんでした → じゃなかった. The plain partner of です is だ. But in speech, especially in questions or before ね / よ, and when women or anyone is speaking softly, だ is often dropped: 元気？ (how are you?), きれいね. Don't put だ in a question (×元気だ？). Because じゃない changes like an い-adjective, its past is じゃなかった. These match the four Tamil forms "மாணவன் தான்" (is a student) / "மாணவன் இல்லை" (is not a student) / "மாணவனாக இருந்தான்" (was a student) / "மாணவனாக இல்லை" (was not a student).
g20-4.tamil_parallel_en: Like the four Tamil forms: ஓய்வு தான் / ஓய்வு இல்லை / ஓய்வாக இருந்தது / ஓய்வாக இல்லை ("free / not free / was free / wasn't free") = 暇だ / 暇じゃない / 暇だった / 暇じゃなかった.
g20-4.formation_en: です→だ (暇です→暇だ、学生です→学生だ) ; じゃありません→じゃない ; でした→だった ; じゃありませんでした→じゃなかった. In questions and before ね/よ, だ is usually dropped (元気？、本当？)
g20-4.pitfalls_en: Don't add だ in a question as in ×暇だ？; say ○暇？. For a な-adjective, it is not ×静かくない but ○静かじゃない.

g20-5.explanation_en: To ask a question in the plain style, drop か and raise your voice at the end of the sentence (written with ？): 行きますか → 行く？. Adding か in the plain style (行くか？) sounds harsh and masculine, so avoid it. Answers: はい → うん (yeah), いいえ → ううん (nope). It is just like raising your voice with the "-ஆ" ending in Tamil "வர்றியா?" (you coming?); in plain Japanese there is not even an ending, only your voice shows it is a question. For an invitation, 〜ませんか → ない-form + ？ (見ない？ = shall we watch it?). Questions with question words work the same way: どこへ行く？、何を食べた？
g20-5.tamil_parallel_en: Like Tamil casual questions with a rising "-ஆ" (Japanese uses only the rising voice): நாளைக்கு வர்றியா? — ஆமா, வர்றேன் ("you coming tomorrow? Yeah, I'm coming") = 明日来る？— うん、来る.
g20-5.formation_en: Polite: 〜ますか / 〜ですか → Plain: dictionary/ない/た form + ？ (rising voice), な-adj/N + ？ (without だ) ; はい → うん、いいえ → ううん ; 〜ませんか (invitation) → 〜ない？
g20-5.pitfalls_en: In the plain style, use うん / ううん instead of はい / いいえ. Watch the length: ううん (no) vs うん (yes), like Tamil "உம்" (yes) / "ஊஹூம்" (no).

g20-6.explanation_en: けど = "but". Like が (〜ですが) from Lesson 8, it joins two contrasting ideas, but it is used more in spoken language. It can come after a plain form (高いけど) or after a polite form (高いですけど). With a な-adjective or noun in the plain style, it is だけど (暇だけど). It matches the spoken Tamil "ஆனா" (but) in "விலை அதிகம், ஆனா ரொம்ப நல்லா இருக்கு" (it's expensive, but it's really good). It is also used to start something softly: ちょっと聞きたいけど… (I wanted to ask you something…).
g20-6.tamil_parallel_en: A direct match for spoken Tamil "ஆனா" (but): விலை அதிகம், ஆனா ரொம்ப ருசி ("it's expensive, but really tasty") = 高いけど、とてもおいしい.
g20-6.formation_en: Plain form + けど (行くけど、高いけど、暇だけど、学生だけど) ; Polite: 〜ですが / 〜ますが ≈ 〜ですけど / 〜ますけど
g20-6.pitfalls_en: With a な-adjective or noun, it is not ×暇けど but ○暇だけど. けど does not give a reason; for a reason, use から.

g20-7.explanation_en: When talking with friends, particles such as は、を、へ and が are often dropped if the meaning is clear: ご飯を食べる？ → ご飯、食べる？; 私は行かない → 私、行かない; 学校へ行く → 学校、行く. Spoken Tamil does the same, dropping "-ஐ" in "சாப்பாடு சாப்பிட்டியா?" (did you eat food?) or shortening to "நான் வரல" (I'm not coming), so this feels natural to Tamil speakers. But で (place / tool)、に (time / destination)、から、まで and と are usually not dropped, because the meaning would change. In writing, in the polite style and in test answers, always write the particles correctly.
g20-7.tamil_parallel_en: Like dropping case endings in spoken Tamil: சாப்பாடு(ஐ) சாப்பிட்டியா? ("did you eat (your) food?") = ご飯(を)食べた？ ; நான் போகல ("I'm not going") = 私(は)行かない.
g20-7.formation_en: Can be dropped: は・を・へ・が (when the meaning is clear) ; Should not be dropped: で・に・から・まで・と ; Polite: ご飯を 食べましたか → Plain: ご飯、食べた？
g20-7.pitfalls_en: Dropping particles like で or に makes the meaning unclear: in バスで行く (I'll go by bus), で is required. When you see a sentence with a dropped particle in the test, fill in the missing particle in your head as you read.

items.L20-q01: 今朝 = けさ (இன்று காலை, this morning); this is a special reading. If you read 今 = いま and 朝 = あさ separately, you get the wrong answer いまあさ.
items.L20-q02: 天気 = てんき (வானிலை, weather). でんき is 電気 (மின்சாரம், electricity); watch the voicing mark.
items.L20-q03: 疲れる = つかれる (களைப்படைய, to get tired); its た-form is つかれた. Don't add voicing marks as in つがれた / づかれた.
items.L20-q04: げんき = 元気 (நலம், well / healthy). 完 (かん) is a look-alike with 宀 on top; 汽 and 木 are sound / shape traps.
items.L20-q05: ひま = 暇 (ஓய்வு, free time). 暖 (あたたかい) and 曜 (ようび) are look-alike kanji with 日 on the left; 眼 has 目 on the left.
items.L20-q06: The reason you can't sleep is the noise (うるさい, சத்தமான). つまらない (சலிப்பான, boring) doesn't stop you sleeping.
items.L20-q07: "Not interesting at all" (கொஞ்சம் கூட சுவாரசியமில்லை) = つまらない (சலிப்பான, boring). うるさい (சத்தமான, noisy) doesn't fit the meaning.
items.L20-q08: "I'll go out with my family" (குடும்பத்துடன் வெளியே கிளம்புவேன்) = 出かける. 要る (தேவைப்பட, to need) doesn't fit with a place.
items.L20-q09: "What do you need?" (என்ன தேவை?) = 何が要る？ (要る = いる, தேவைப்பட, to need). Don't confuse 要る with 居る (இருக்க, to exist, for living things); both are read いる, but 要る is Group I (要らない).
items.L20-q10: Which of two: in the plain style, どっち (எது, which one; polite: どちら). どれ is for choosing among three or more.
items.L20-q11: I asked my elder brother for help = 頼んだ (கேட்டேன், the た-form of 頼む). 会った (சந்தித்தேன், met) does not take を.
items.L20-q12: 暇 (ஓய்வு, free) = 忙しくない (வேலை அதிகம் இல்லை, not busy). 休みじゃない (it's not a holiday) leans towards the opposite meaning.
items.L20-q13: 会わなかった = 会いませんでした (சந்திக்கவில்லை, didn't meet): plain → polite. 会いました is the opposite meaning.
items.L20-q14: The plain question 本当？ = the polite 本当ですか (உண்மையா?, really?). 本当です without ？ is not a question but a statement.
items.L20-q15: ううん (இல்லை, no) + tomorrow (future) = 行かない (போக மாட்டேன், won't go). 行かなかった is past and doesn't fit with "tomorrow".
items.L20-q16: The plain past of an い-adjective: 寒い → 寒かった (குளிராக இருந்தது, was cold). 寒いだった / 寒いだ are wrong; don't add だ to an い-adjective.
items.L20-q17: "Yesterday" calls for the past negative: 楽しく + なかった (மகிழ்ச்சியாக இல்லை, wasn't fun). じゃなかった is only for な-adjectives and nouns.
items.L20-q18: The plain past of a な-adjective: 静か + だった (அமைதியாக இருந்தது, was quiet). 静かかった wrongly applies the い-adjective rule.
items.L20-q19: The plain negative of a noun: 学生 + じゃない (மாணவன் இல்லை, not a student). 学生くない / 学生ない are wrong forms.
items.L20-q20: Expensive ↔ tasty: the contrasting link "but" (ஆனால்) = けど. から (ஏனென்றால், because) gives a reason and doesn't fit.
items.L20-q21: な-adjective + けど needs だ in the middle: 暇だけど (ஓய்வு தான், ஆனால், I'm free, but). 暇けど / 暇なけど are wrong.
items.L20-q22: 今晩 みんなで 映画 見ない？ A plain invitation: ない-form + ？ (polite: 見ませんか); を has been dropped (映画[を]).
items.L20-q23: 疲れたけど、旅行は とても 楽しかった。 けど attaches to the first clause; then the topic + は, the adverb, and the past form of the い-adjective.
items.L20-q24: 昨日は どこへも 行かなかったよ。 "どこへも + negative" (Lesson 5) in the plain form: 行きませんでした → 行かなかった.
items.L20-q25: [1] In a plain question, no だ: 暇？. [2] "I'd like to see the film, but I'm a bit tired…" (படம் பார்க்கலாம், ஆனால் கொஞ்சம் களைப்பு…): a soft refusal with けど. [3] "Last week" calls for the past negative of an い-adjective: 面白く + なかった; じゃなかった is only for な-adjectives.
